instruction:
Work in the container in the repository checked out at /dateutil (a dateutil 2.6.0 source tree). Fix TWO bugs, both in /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py. The hidden tests that must pass are `dateutil.test.test_rrule.RRuleTest::testCountZero` and `dateutil.test.test_rrule.RRuleTest::testStrAppendRRULEToken`. Those tests are NOT in the repository; their names describe the expected behaviour:
 - testCountZero: `rrule(..., count=0, ...)` must yield zero occurrences (count=0 means an empty recurrence set, not 'no count limit'), i.e. `list(rrule(DAILY, count=0, dtstart=...)) == []` and `rrule(DAILY, count=0, dtstart=...).count() == 0`.
 - testStrAppendRRULEToken: `str(rrule(...))` must output a string that can be fed back into `rrulestr()`; in particular the RRULE part must be prefixed with the `RRULE:` token, i.e. `str(rrule(DAILY, count=3, dtstart=datetime(1997,9,2,9,0)))` should be `'DTSTART:19970902T090000\nRRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3'` (the existing in-repo helper `_rrulestr_reverse_test` round-trips str(rule) through rrulestr and must keep working; note `rrulestr` accepts a bare `FREQ=...` value line too, so check carefully which form the class docstring/`__str__` docstring promises: '__str__: Output a string that would generate this RRULE if passed to rrulestr').

Rules: you MUST NOT edit or delete any existing test file (dateutil/test/*), and you MUST NOT break any currently-passing test (in particular the many `testToStr*` tests that call `_rrulestr_reverse_test`, and the `testStr*` rrulestr tests). Do not add new features. Only fix bugs in dateutil/rrule.py.

Method suggestions: read `__str__`, `_iter`, `_parse_rfc`, `_parse_rfc_rrule`, `rrulestr`, and the `count`/`_count` handling. Note that `if self._count:` and `if count:` are falsy for 0. Also check `replace()`, `__len__`/`count()`, `xafter`, `between`, and the COUNT= output. Be careful: fixing count=0 must not change behaviour when count is None.

Before changing anything run: `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q 2>&1 | tail -3` and record the result. After your fix run the same command and make sure no pre-existing test fails.

Report back: the exact file/lines, each bug, the fixes (show the diff), the evidence (commands + outputs), and confirmation that the full test suite still passes.

Work in the container in the repository checked out at /dateutil (a dateutil 2.6.0 source tree). Fix ONE bug: the hidden test `dateutil.test.test_parser.ParserTest::testFuzzyWithTokens` must pass. That test is NOT in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour (parsing with `fuzzy_with_tokens=True`). There is a bug in /dateutil/dateutil/parser.py that makes that test fail.

Rules: you MUST NOT edit or delete any existing test file (dateutil/test/*), and you MUST NOT break any currently-passing test. Do not add new features. Only fix the bug in dateutil/parser.py.

Method suggestions: study `_parse` and `parse` in dateutil/parser.py, especially the `fuzzy_with_tokens` code path (the `l` list of tokens, the `skip` indices, the returned tuple `(res, skipped_tokens)`). `parse('1am July 15, 2013', fuzzy_with_tokens=True)` should return a (datetime, tuple-of-ignored-substrings) pair whose concatenation reconstructs the input; check that the returned tokens are exactly the non-date substrings and that they are returned in the right order/type (tuple of str), and that `fuzzy_with_tokens` works together with `fuzzy=True` and with timezone/`default` arguments. Look for an injected/incorrect line (e.g. wrong index, wrong slicing, returning a list instead of tuple, or the wrong variable).

Before changing anything run: `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q 2>&1 | tail -3` and record the result. After your fix run the same command and make sure no pre-existing test fails.

Report back: the exact file/line, the bug, the fix (show the diff), the evidence (commands + outputs), and confirmation that the full test suite still passes.

Work in the container in the repository checked out at /dateutil (a dateutil 2.6.0 source tree). Fix ONE bug: the hidden test `dateutil.test.test_relativedelta.RelativeDeltaTest::testAdditionFloatValue` must pass. That test is NOT in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour (addition of a relativedelta containing float/fractional relative values). There is a bug in /dateutil/dateutil/relativedelta.py that makes that test fail.

Rules: you MUST NOT edit or delete any existing test file (dateutil/test/*), and you MUST NOT break any currently-passing test. Do not add new features. Only fix the bug in dateutil/relativedelta.py.

Method suggestions: read the whole file; the class docstring documents expected behaviour of relativedelta arithmetic. Compare `dt + relativedelta(days=1.5)`, `dt + relativedelta(days=1.5, hours=2)`, `dt + relativedelta(months=1, days=1.5)`, `dt + relativedelta(weeks=1.5)`, `dt + relativedelta(seconds=1.5)`, `date + relativedelta(...)`, `relativedelta + relativedelta`, `relativedelta + timedelta`, `rd * 2`, `rd / 2`, `rd.normalized()` against the mathematically expected results (a fractional relativedelta of N days must equal timedelta(days=N)). Write randomized property tests comparing `dt + rd` with `dt + timedelta(...)` and `rd.normalized()` with the equivalent integer relativedelta. Look for an injected/incorrect line (e.g. a wrong attribute, a missing fractional carry, a wrong rounding, a wrong comparison).

Before changing anything run: `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q 2>&1 | tail -3` and record the result (it should be all passing). After your fix run the same command and make sure the number of failures/passes is unchanged (no pre-existing test may fail).

Report back: the exact file/line, the bug, the one-line fix (show the diff), the evidence (commands + outputs) that the behaviour is now correct, and confirmation that the full test suite still passes.
